program_title: TRAINING PROGRAM: NEW SUPPORT AGENT ONBOARDING (WEEK ONE)
target_learners: New customer support agents at a SaaS company; about 40 people in cohorts.
Entry: basic computer skills and written English; no support experience required.
general_objective: Equip new agents to handle customer tickets independently by the end of the first week, within the SLA and the quality rubric.

knowledge: Describe the ticket life cycle, SLA, product and escalation rules;
skills: Resolve, answer and escalate tickets in the helpdesk to the quality rubric;
autonomy: Take responsibility for their own queue and ask for help at the right time.

modules.title: Support foundations and the ticket workflow
modules.position: First module of the program. It comes before all ticket-handling modules.
modules.nature: Required module that integrates knowledge and skill; builds the ability to run one ticket through the helpdesk.

knowledge: Describe the support team structure, service levels (SLA) and ticket life cycle;
skills: Process a ticket from queue to closure in the helpdesk tool within the SLA;
autonomy: Comply with the team's SLA and tagging rules on every ticket.

lessons.title: Support team, SLA and ticket life cycle

objectives.knowledge: List the ticket statuses and the SLA target of each priority level without notes.
objectives.skills: Set priority and status on 5 sandbox tickets, all correct against the SLA table.
objectives.autonomy: Comply with the SLA table when setting priority on every ticket.

content: 3. Practice: set status and priority on 5 sandbox tickets

lessons.title: Working the queue in the helpdesk tool

objectives.knowledge: Describe the filters, views, tags and macros used in the helpdesk tool.
objectives.skills: Work 8 sandbox tickets from queue to closure in 90 minutes, with correct tags and at least one macro each.
objectives.autonomy: Take initiative to flag a mis-tagged ticket to the team lead.

conditions.learning_space: Live online classroom (video conference) with breakout rooms.
conditions.equipment: Laptop with webcam and headset, stable Internet, access to the training helpdesk sandbox.
conditions.materials: Sandbox ticket queue, macro library, scenario cards, scoring rubric.
conditions.other_resources: A senior agent as co-facilitator and the internal knowledge base.

content.skills: Ticket queue worked in the sandbox.
content.autonomy: Compliance with SLA and tagging rules.

assessment.method: Formative: facilitator checks the sandbox queue against a checklist.

guidelines.scope: For all new support agents in the onboarding cohort.
guidelines.instructor: Demonstrate live in the sandbox, then run timed practice rounds in breakout rooms and give feedback against the rubric.
guidelines.learners: Join the live session with camera on, work tickets in the sandbox, review a peer's replies.
key_points: Every reply is checked against the rubric before it is sent;
Learners work real-style tickets, not slides.

references: Internal support playbook and knowledge base of the company (current version).

modules.title: Product knowledge and troubleshooting
modules.position: Follows M01. Prepares for writing customer replies in M03.
modules.nature: Required module integrating product knowledge and diagnostic skill.

knowledge: Describe the core product features, plans and common failure points;
skills: Diagnose a customer problem and resolve it using the knowledge base and product sandbox;
autonomy: Verify the fix with the customer before closing a ticket.

lessons.title: Core product features and plans

objectives.knowledge: Describe the 6 core features and the 3 plan tiers and which limits apply to each.
objectives.skills: Reproduce 5 typical customer scenarios in the product sandbox.
objectives.autonomy: Take responsibility for checking the customer's plan before suggesting a feature.

content: 3. Practice: reproduce 5 customer scenarios in the sandbox

objectives.knowledge: List the diagnostic questions for login, billing and integration issues.
objectives.skills: Resolve 6 sandbox tickets using the knowledge base, with steps that a customer can follow, in 20 minutes each.
objectives.autonomy: Cooperate with the senior agent when a root cause is unclear.

conditions.learning_space: Live online classroom with product sandbox.
conditions.equipment: Laptop with webcam and headset, stable Internet, access to the training helpdesk sandbox.
conditions.materials: Sandbox ticket queue, macro library, scenario cards, scoring rubric.
conditions.other_resources: A senior agent as co-facilitator and the internal knowledge base.

assessment.method: Practical test: resolve 3 unseen sandbox tickets scored with a rubric.

guidelines.scope: For all new support agents in the onboarding cohort.
guidelines.instructor: Demonstrate live in the sandbox, then run timed practice rounds in breakout rooms and give feedback against the rubric.
guidelines.learners: Join the live session with camera on, work tickets in the sandbox, review a peer's replies.
key_points: Every reply is checked against the rubric before it is sent;
Learners work real-style tickets, not slides.

references: Internal support playbook and knowledge base of the company (current version).

modules.title: Customer communication in writing and live chat
modules.position: Follows M02. It applies product knowledge to real replies.
modules.nature: Required module building the competency of writing clear, empathetic replies.

knowledge: State the structure of an effective support reply and the tone rules of the company;
skills: Write replies and live-chat responses that meet the quality rubric;
autonomy: Show care and a calm tone with frustrated customers.

lessons.title: Writing clear and empathetic replies

objectives.knowledge: State the 5 parts of a support reply and the tone rules.
objectives.skills: Write 6 email replies from scenario cards, each scoring at least 4 of 5 on the rubric.
objectives.autonomy: Exercise care in tone on every reply.

content: 3. Practice: write 6 replies and peer-review them

objectives.knowledge: Describe techniques for de-escalating an angry customer.
objectives.skills: Handle 3 live chat role-plays, keeping the customer calm and resolving the issue within 10 minutes.
objectives.autonomy: Remain calm under pressure during role-plays.

conditions.learning_space: Live online classroom with breakout pairs.
conditions.equipment: Laptop with webcam and headset, stable Internet, access to the training helpdesk sandbox.
conditions.materials: Sandbox ticket queue, macro library, scenario cards, scoring rubric.
conditions.other_resources: A senior agent as co-facilitator and the internal knowledge base.

assessment.method: Rubric-scored test: 2 written replies and 1 live-chat role-play.

guidelines.scope: For all new support agents in the onboarding cohort.
guidelines.instructor: Demonstrate live in the sandbox, then run timed practice rounds in breakout rooms and give feedback against the rubric.
guidelines.learners: Join the live session with camera on, work tickets in the sandbox, review a peer's replies.
key_points: Every reply is checked against the rubric before it is sent;
Learners work real-style tickets, not slides.

references: Internal support playbook and knowledge base of the company (current version).

modules.title: Escalation, handoff and independent handling
modules.position: Last module. It combines M01 to M03 into independent work.
modules.nature: Required integrated module ending with a supervised solo shift.

knowledge: Describe the escalation criteria and the handoff template;
skills: Escalate a ticket with a complete handoff note and handle a supervised solo queue;
autonomy: Take responsibility for own queue and ask for help at the right time.

objectives.knowledge: List the escalation criteria for bugs, security and billing disputes.
objectives.skills: Write 4 handoff notes with all required fields, each accepted by the receiving team without questions.
objectives.autonomy: Take initiative to escalate when criteria are met.

objectives.knowledge: Describe how own queue performance is measured.
objectives.skills: Handle a live-style queue of 12 tickets alone in 2 hours with 90 percent meeting SLA.
objectives.autonomy: Take responsibility for the quality of every ticket sent.

conditions.learning_space: Live online classroom plus supervised sandbox shift.
conditions.equipment: Laptop with webcam and headset, stable Internet, access to the training helpdesk sandbox.
conditions.materials: Sandbox ticket queue, macro library, scenario cards, scoring rubric.
conditions.other_resources: A senior agent as co-facilitator and the internal knowledge base.

content.skills: Solo queue result and handoff notes.

assessment.method: Final practical: supervised solo queue scored with the rubric.

guidelines.scope: For all new support agents in the onboarding cohort.
guidelines.instructor: Demonstrate live in the sandbox, then run timed practice rounds in breakout rooms and give feedback against the rubric.
guidelines.learners: Join the live session with camera on, work tickets in the sandbox, review a peer's replies.
key_points: Every reply is checked against the rubric before it is sent;
Learners work real-style tickets, not slides.

references: Internal support playbook and knowledge base of the company (current version).

sections.heading: 1.1. Admission
items: Admit all new support hires; cohorts of up to 20 per live group.

sections.heading: 1.2. Delivery
items: Mostly live online sessions over five days, with a sandbox helpdesk.

sections.heading: 1.3. Assessment and certification
items: Learners attend at least 80% of hours; each module is scored 10-point scale; 7.0 needed to join the live queue.

sections.heading: 1.4. Credit transfer and recognition of prior learning

implementation_guidelines.heading: 2. Requirements for the training provider
items: Facilitator with 1 year of support experience.
Sandbox helpdesk available for each learner.
